questions.previous: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.
questions.text: Important national policy decisions should be delegated to independent experts who do not need approval from elected representatives for each decision.

questions.previous: The head of government should be able to enact national laws even when parliament votes against them.
questions.text: During a serious emergency, the head of government should be able to put temporary laws into effect before parliament votes, with those laws expiring if parliament rejects them.

questions.previous: Opposition representatives should be able to investigate the government’s use of public money.
questions.text: Citizens should be able to put proposed national laws to a binding public vote by collecting enough signatures.

questions.previous: National governments should be chosen by trade union leaders rather than by the general electorate.
questions.text: The governing party or coalition should be able to choose a new head of government between elections without holding a new public vote.

questions.previous: National leaders should have sole authority over major national policy decisions.
questions.text: An elected head of government should be able to make major policy decisions within existing law without obtaining parliament’s approval for each decision.

questions.previous: A national leader should be able to postpone scheduled elections without independent approval when they consider political continuity necessary.
questions.text: Parliament should be able to postpone a scheduled national election during a serious emergency, for a limited period specified in law.

limitation: Owner-defined broader construct, not empirical population calibration. Six questions independently reassessed; no target distribution or score adjustment.
